answer: Sybil resistance comes from making coordination costly, not merely counting identities: when k bonded identities equivocate in a correlated pattern, the penalty grows as O(k²), debiting their shared collateral escrow. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier with base greater than one, so a larger swarm risks sharply greater loss. Asymmetric depreciation prevents recovery from erasing the cost; labels such as vine, sable, and forge do not create independent economic safety.
